### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via innerRefusal (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), innerRefusal (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via describeEffectiveAccess (sdk, the bare tail of client method security.describeEffectiveAccess, bound to GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/effective-access))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), innerRefusal (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), userMessage (symbol, a field of interface StrandedDecisionDetails), innerRefusal (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal), userMessage (literal, a string literal in ResumeRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via describeEffectiveAccess (sdk, the bare tail of client method security.describeEffectiveAccess, bound to GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/effective-access))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 97defd60674b4b7dc795c0e30103818020a6f2c9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `014882d3a5fdb388a6bab6f2ed2a439d9789cd1d` — the merge of head `95eae72668321d7f8eb2233f80753911e1202288` into base `97defd60674b4b7dc795c0e30103818020a6f2c9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 014882d3a5fdb388a6bab6f2ed2a439d9789cd1d && git checkout 014882d3a5fdb388a6bab6f2ed2a439d9789cd1d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 97defd60674b4b7dc795c0e30103818020a6f2c9 95eae72668321d7f8eb2233f80753911e1202288 && git checkout -B drift-repro 97defd60674b4b7dc795c0e30103818020a6f2c9 && git merge --no-ff 95eae72668321d7f8eb2233f80753911e1202288

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 97defd60674b4b7dc795c0e30103818020a6f2c9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 97defd60674b4b7dc795c0e30103818020a6f2c9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34619 · card #34579 · first review · L1-c of seat repo:objectstack#2 · read 2026-11-17T04:24Z

Head-sha: `95eae72668321d7f8eb2233f80753911e1202288` (the head of final-head report 6938126740)

Read from GitHub at this head (`get`, the diff, check-runs) and from the tree at this head, not from the report.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`. The body opens with the attribution lines, then `Fixes #34579`. No other card number sits next to a closing verb. 10 files, +458/−6.
- Scope against the narrowed acceptance (premise correction 6936860860): the approver gets the refusal in the 500 answer, the decision stays recorded and repairable (#13807 B, #13937 shape 4 untouched), and a fault edge on that step does not strand. Each of the three is delivered and pinned (below). The card body's preferred route (a 4xx with the request left pending) is not delivered, and the seat recorded why. See D1.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, in the body and the changeset. The title has no `!`, which is right for a widening. All three packages are `patch`, which is right for `none` (AGENTS.md checklist step 3). No `content/docs/releases/`.
- Code, line by line:
  - `serviceResume` used to drop the engine's `innerRefusal` / `userMessage`. It now keeps them on the thrown error as `resumeRefusal`, beside `resumeCode` / `resumeStatus`, and copies them only when the engine reported them.
  - `resumeRecordedOutcome` spreads `resumeRefusalOf(err)` into the one `strandedDecisionFailure` throw. That is the only call site in `plugin-approvals` (`approval-service.ts:6295`), so every decision door that resumes through it carries the members.
  - `strandedDecisionDetails` keeps the four facts all-or-nothing, as before. It then adds `innerRefusal` only when `code` parses as `ErrorCode` and `message` is a string. That matches `FlowInnerRefusalSchema` (`automation-api.zod.ts:363`) member for member. It adds `userMessage` through the existing `declaredUserMessage` (a non-blank string). A malformed member is dropped and the facts stand. `@objectstack/types` already depends on `@objectstack/spec` and already imports `ErrorCode` from `spec/api` in `thrown-http-error.ts`, so this adds no dependency edge.
  - `rest`: no logic change. `handleApprovalError` already spreads the recognised envelope at the top level for `RESUME_FAILED` only, and only the comment is new.
  - The engine side is not touched. Its failure exits already spread `readCarriedRefusal(err)` (`engine.ts:8553`, `dag-traversal.ts:1658`, `run-resume.ts`), and `refusalCarriedBy` brands any throw that declares a status in 400–499 (`inner-refusal.ts:90`). So the changeset's "a declared refusal, a validation rule, a permission" holds for every 4xx-declared refusal, and a fault (no declared status) carries nothing.
- Published text: the changeset, the `approvals.mdx` callout and the `ApprovalDecisionResult.resumed` docblock were read sentence by sentence against the code and the pins. "Both are absent when the run met a fault rather than a refusal" is pinned by the reverse control. "draw a `fault` edge … the decision then answers normally" is pinned by case 2. The `spec` edit is comment-only: no schema, `.describe()` or generated artifact moves.
- Tests:
  - `hook-refusal-after-decision.test.ts` is new. It uses the real `AutomationEngine`, the real `update_record` and approval nodes, and a data double that throws in `resolveHookRefusal`'s shape.
    - Case 1: no fault edge. It asserts `RESUME_FAILED`, the decision still `approved` and the plan still `submitted`, and that the details equal the four facts plus both members.
    - Case 2: a fault edge. The handler runs, `resumed: true`, and nothing is left parked.
    - Case 3, reverse control: a fault, so neither member appears.
    - Ablation (source reverted to `origin/main`): case 1 is red, and cases 2 and 3 stay green. That is expected, because case 2 pins existing engine routing.
  - `rest`: a new exact-key-set pin on the 500 body. The #13807 key-set pins are unchanged.
  - `types`: round-trip; five malformed shapes each dropped while the facts stand, with the well-formed reverse control; and a refusal member never rescues a partial envelope.
  - No existing test was changed. The `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` entries are the new double's two verbs.
- Gates: 72 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 60 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 0 failed. `success` includes Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (8/8), Test UI (16/16), Type Check UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset and PR-body guards (both re-run after the 04:15Z body edit), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Build Docs and Check Documentation Links. The local reconciliation: 125 derived gates run, all exit 0, 0 NOT-MEASURED.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. **No leak is added on the 5xx.** `innerRefusal.message` is the same diagnostic text the flow doors already serve in `FLOW_FAILED` details (ruling B′ on #24914), and `error` already carried the reason's prose. `userMessage` is present only where the producer marked it, which is the 5xx-safe channel ADR-0112 reads.
2. **The recogniser cannot let an unvetted value through.** `serviceResume` copies the engine's members unvalidated. The only path to the wire is `strandedDecisionDetails`, which rebuilds `{ code, message }` from parsed values and drops any extra key. The `types` cases pin a non-ledger code, a missing message, a bare string, a blank `userMessage` and a non-string `userMessage`.

**Deviations recorded (not L1 defects)**
- D1: the card's preferred route is not delivered (a dry-run, then a 4xx, with the request left pending), and neither is the "refusal visible on the request" alternative. The refusal is carried in the 500 answer only and is not stored on the request row. `Fixes` closes the card on the seat's narrowed acceptance (6936860860), whose "at least" arm (route down a declared failure edge) is met. Reopening #13807 B is the maintainer's call, as the seat recorded.
- D2: `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`. AGENTS.md does not require this line for `none` with a widening, but the PR declares it. Per the pm-dispatch rule, the seat files the owed card and rewrites the line to `follow-up #N` before landing.

**L2 owed: yes.** It is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because of `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (a published error envelope gains two members) and the non-test `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` path (comment only). The opus review seat claimed it at 04:19Z (l2-review#4). No record is on this head yet.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34619` reports NOT governed, +458/−6 = 464 lines ≤ 3000. After the L2 PASS on this head and the D2 line rewrite, the area lands it through the ordinary queue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `95eae72668321d7f8eb2233f80753911e1202288`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/types/src/stranded-decision.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts

Inputs read: card #34579 (body and all four comments, including premise correction 6936860860 and the final-head report 6938126740), PR #34619 (body, file list, net diff against `main` from merge base `8dd8192c`), and the check-runs on this head. The remainder of the diff (three test files, `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, the changeset prose, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the pin ledger and the changeset level are answered below because the seat asked.

Check-runs on this head: every completed run concluded `success` or `skipped`, including Test Core shards 1/8 through 8/8, TypeScript Type Check (workspace, source, consumer, debt ledger), all Lint families, Check Changeset (both runs), Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Build Docs, and Test UI 1/16 through 16/16. One run is still pending and is not a verdict: the aggregate job `Test Core` (in progress); its eight shards are all green.

### ① Derived judgments

- `StrandedDecisionDetails` (`@objectstack/types`) gains two optional members, `innerRefusal?: FlowInnerRefusal` and `userMessage?: string`. Right: both are optional, the four #13807 facts keep their all-or-nothing rule, and the type of `innerRefusal` is the spec's existing `FlowInnerRefusal`, no new vocabulary.
- `strandedDecisionDetails` (the recogniser) used to return exactly four keys; it now returns four to six. Right: a carrier it accepted before is still accepted with the same four values; a carrier it refused before (a missing or malformed fact) is still refused, and a refusal member never rescues it (the head's own pin, green in CI). A malformed optional member is dropped without dropping the facts. Nothing previously accepted now refuses.
- Wire: `500 RESUME_FAILED` on the approvals decision doors gains two optional top-level body keys, present only when the engine reported them. Right: status, `code`, the `error` prose and the four facts are byte-for-byte what `main` answers; the REST handler has no logic change (it already spreads the recognised envelope), and the no-refusal body keeps its exact six-key set (existing pin unchanged and green).
- No existing field changes meaning. `error` is untouched; `repairable` is still derived from the engine's `'stranded'` status alone.
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` moves a docblock only: no schema, no exported member, no generated artifact. Right, and consistent with green Spec property liveness and type-check runs.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains two rows (`update`, `delete`) for the new test file's engine double. This is the honest consequence of adding that double, which routes both verbs through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` and `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`; it is a generated coverage ledger that may only grow, no row was removed, and it is not a consequence of the envelope change itself.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset declares `patch` on `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/rest`. Right under AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Nothing a metadata author can write changes, so `none` is the right kind.
- The declaration `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right, on the PR body and in the changeset body alike: a published envelope gains two optional members, nothing previously accepted refuses, and no envelope field changes meaning.
- `@objectstack/spec` is not named in the changeset although its contracts file moves. Accepted: the move is a comment, and spec sits in the same fixed release group as the three named packages, so it versions with them. Check Changeset concluded `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (route a contract review): answered by this record.
- Open question 2 (`userMessage` beside `innerRefusal`, beyond the premise's wording): option A, carry both, is upheld. The dev's measurement holds in the tree on `main`: `resolveHookRefusal` builds `SandboxError(err.message, answer.message, { code, status, userMessage: answer.message })`, so `.message` stays the wrapper `hook 'NAME' threw: …`; `refusalCarriedBy` sets `innerRefusal.message` from `resolveThrownHttpError(err).message`, which is that `.message`; the declared, localized sentence is only on `.userMessage`. Shipping `innerRefusal` alone would miss the card's narrowed acceptance line (the approver gets the hook's readable refusal).
- Premise note: the seat's premise called `innerRefusal` the hook's localized text; the dev narrowed that by measurement and the narrowing is correct as above.
- Deviation, package suites ran one commit earlier: accepted; the final commit moves only the two test files and the pin ledger, and the check-runs on this head are the verdict.
- Deviation, review request not sent by the dev: no effect on the contract.
- Dev flag `security_findings: none`, and the seat's disclosure question: agreed, no new disclosure. On `main` the same response already returns the same diagnostic text in `error`: the `update_record` arm reports `update_record(OBJECT) failed: ` plus the thrown message, the engine prefixes the node id, `serviceResume` puts that in its error, and `resumeRecordedOutcome` appends it to the `RESUME_FAILED` prose the REST door serves. `innerRefusal.message` is a substring of what the caller already receives, `userMessage` is the hook author's own declared sentence for whoever performs the write, and the flow doors already serve the same pair. A crash (no declared 4xx) carries no `innerRefusal` at all.
- Out-of-scope finding, `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`: the skills text on `main` is not made false. `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` says nothing about `RESUME_FAILED`, stranded runs or the envelope; `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` teaches the flow doors' read order (top-level `userMessage`, then `details.innerRefusal`, then `message`), which stays true and which a client SDK caller can also apply here. The follow-up is additive teaching. The PR names the path but links no card number; the seat should file or link that card before landing.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` (the `hits` file), against the rulings it cites and its first consumer:

- It stays inside #13807 option B and the #13937 shape-4 ruling: the paragraph says neither member moves the status code or the four facts, and the code agrees. The existing prohibition (these facts are not members of `ApprovalDecisionResult` and are not `resumeFailure`) still follows it and still reads correctly with the new paragraph in between.
- `innerRefusal` is described as `{ code, message }`, the engine's `AutomationResult.innerRefusal` under ruling B′ on #24914. That matches `FlowInnerRefusalSchema` on `main` and what `run-resume.ts` spreads on its stranded exit (`...readCarriedRefusal(err)`).
- The fault-edge sentence holds against `dag-traversal.ts` on `main`: a failed node's `fault` edge is followed for every failure except a guard refusal, on both the thrown and the returned-failure arms. The head pins it end to end with a real engine and the real approval and `update_record` nodes, and that file is green in the Test Core shards.
- Carrying both members is right, and the two envelopes agree field by field with `FLOW_FAILED` on `main` (producer: `flowFailureDetails` and `flowFailureEnvelope` in `packages/runtime/src/flow-dispatch-status.ts`; contract: `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` and `AutomationResult` in spec):
  - `innerRefusal`: same type, same producer value, same presence rule (only when a refusal was met, never synthesised). Position differs by dialect only: `error.details.innerRefusal` in the flow doors' nested envelope, a body top-level key beside the four facts in this door's flat `{ code, error }` dialect. Through the client SDK both read as `err.details.innerRefusal`, because the flat body falls through to `err.details`.
  - `userMessage`: same semantics (presence is the marking), same single read (`declaredUserMessage`, unbounded at both doors), top level of the error in both dialects, and the SDK reads the flat body's top-level key first, so both surface as `err.userMessage`.
  - The one asymmetry is older than this PR: `FLOW_FAILED` details have a Zod declaration in spec, while the `RESUME_FAILED` body is declared by the TypeScript interface in `@objectstack/types` plus this docblock, as the four facts already were.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence:

- `packages/types/src/stranded-decision.ts`: agrees. The recogniser validates `code` against the closed `ErrorCode` set and `message` as a string, which is exactly `FlowInnerRefusalSchema`'s shape, and reads `userMessage` through `declaredUserMessage`, so a blank or non-string value is not a marking. Every code the engine can produce here comes from `resolveThrownHttpError` or the ruled unique-violation spelling, so a real refusal is never dropped by the validation. `@objectstack/spec` is already a declared runtime dependency of this package and `ErrorCode` is already imported at runtime one file over, so no dependency edge is added.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`: agrees. `serviceResume` keeps the two members beside `resumeCode` and `resumeStatus` and attaches nothing when the engine reported neither; `resumeRecordedOutcome` spreads them after the four facts, so they cannot overwrite a fact. Every door that resumes through `resumeRecordedOutcome` carries them. The `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` exit and the log line are unchanged.
- `packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts`: agrees. Comment only; the spread is still gated on `code === 'RESUME_FAILED'` and a recognised envelope, and the head pins the exact eight-key body.

Break attempts that did not break it: a carrier with a code outside the ledger, a missing message, a string in place of the object, a blank `userMessage`, and a partial envelope with valid refusal members are all handled as the docblocks say; a fault (no declared status) carries neither member; a test double returning nothing from `resume` is still read as success.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, both left as accepted deviations (a fix on these files would move the head):

- N1 (nit) — the spec paragraph, and the changeset after it, say both members are absent when the run met a fault. `refusalCarriedBy` reads `userMessage` off any throw that marked one, whether or not its declared status is in the 400 range, while `innerRefusal` needs a declared status in that range, so `userMessage` can in principle be present alone. Each member is declared optional on its own and the `@objectstack/types` docblock states the exact rule (absent when the run met no marked refusal), so no consumer branch is wrong; the wording inherits the same looseness from `AutomationResult.userMessage` on `main`.
- N2 (nit) — the refusal reaches only the thrown envelope. The recall door and the subflow-parent strand report a stranded run on a success answer through `resumeFailure`, which carries no refusal. That is outside this card and the spec text already separates the two channels; a follow-up card can decide whether `ResumeFailureReport` should carry the same pair.

Observation outside the diff, not a finding on this head: `innerRefusal.message` for a sandboxed hook is the debug wrapper naming the hook, at this door and at the flow doors alike, where the data doors answer the hook's own sentence in `message`. That is ruling B′'s existing behaviour on `main`; the marked `userMessage` is what makes the answer readable, which is why carrying it here is necessary.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xczkxx`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmP44onN8RMzsPMqjRq`

**VERDICT: PASS**
